svg.title: Radioactive decay
svg.desc: The number of radioactive nuclei, N, starting from 1,000,000, versus time in multiples of the half-life t1/2. Each half-life halves the number: 500,000 after one half-life, 250,000 after two, 125,000 after three, down to 977 after ten. The curve is an exponential decay, and a table beside it lists the values. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Half of the expected survivors remain after each half-life
A fixed seeded sample of 80 independent lifetimes fluctuates around N = N0 × 2^(−t/t½). A gray dot
has decayed; the blue curve is the ensemble expectation.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
